page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and custom ARMv9 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs using the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It lacks local storage and integrated GPUs, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core and multi-core Geekbench tests, software compilation with Clang, and text processing. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also place in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are rated as strong. Memory performance is highlighted by a top-tier Passmark memory score and strong cached read-only memory bandwidth, though uncached large-block read and write operations fall into the average category.

For specialized workloads, the c9g.8xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in database operations and static web serving throughput, alongside strong Redis SET operation rates. Large language model inference speeds for a small 135M model are strong for prompt processing and average for text generation, while medium 7B model inference remains average. Given the dedicated ARMv9 core allocation and high memory bandwidth efficiency, this instance offers a high-density compute profile for compilation, database hosting, web serving, and parallelized data processing tasks without the overhead of hyperthreading.
